note: The obstacle stack's gap cue in flight (visual_brain --obstacle-stack on|shadow; off by default). 'pilot': haltere.liftoff.gap_aim.GapAimConfig, how the fast pilot confirms and applies the per-frame gap-cue shift. 'runtime': where the camera stack runs the relative depth and haltere.vision.gap_cue, and which declared response model (configs/obstacles/response_models.json, near_on_path) each fast motor contract uses. Version 5 keeps every version 2 value and adds side commitment near an obstacle and two terrain-vote rules (see 'change' and 'pilot_notes'); the runtime refuses other versions (gap_stack.GAP_PILOT_VERSION). The hash covers everything except frozen/frozen_at/sha256; a change needs a new version and a new freeze before any live flight, and every version flown is reported.

pilot_notes.active_deg: the gap cue's own episode threshold (configs/obstacles/gap_cue.json active_deg)
pilot_notes.max_shift_deg: the gap cue's shift clip; the bound of the gap aim's own offset beside the ring. With lag-aware turns (configs/obstacles/lag_turn.json version 2) the lead is computed on the bearing without the gap shift and the shift is added after it, never amplified: during a lag-turn window the flown aim can be up to course_lead_max_deg (15) + max_shift_deg (12) deg from the ring cue's own aim
pilot_notes.conflict_deg: a sample whose ring azimuth differs from the ring cue's by more than this describes another ring (a checkpoint switch, or a sample from a frame before it); between consecutive frames at 6 m/s the ring bearing moves about 1 deg at 20 m and about 2.5 deg at 3 m
pilot_notes.flag_conflict_deg: the ring cue's flag clearance (aim_u beside the ring centre, haltere.vision.race_cues.flag_clearance) counts from this offset; the opposite side to the gap shift is a conflict and the ring cue's own aim is held
pilot_notes.terrain: terrain side steer: only while the looming TTC governor requests a climb (expansion below the flight path); |ln(L/R)| >= terrain_lr (ratio 1.5, the design study's terrain_side.py trigger) votes terrain_side_deg (half the shift clip) toward the farther side
pilot_notes.commit: side commitment near an obstacle: an obstacle confirmation (2 of 3 samples, as before) commits to its side when one of its confirming samples reports one-sided evidence of a close obstacle: near_on_path (a near column on the path the vehicle is committed to over the cue's 1 s path horizon, from the motor's declared response model) in a decision that is not 'occluded' (commit_occluded). While committed the target stays on that side with the largest confirming |shift| since the commitment (no decay, clipped to max_shift_deg); while the obstacle is still ahead the hold is refreshed: by an obstacle vote for either side (an opposite vote does not move the target and switches only under switch_votes / switch_window_s) or a valid close sample; terrain votes are ignored; ring and flag conflicts release it as before (the checkpoint switched: the ring was passed)
pilot_notes.commit_hold_s: released when no refreshing evidence arrived for this long (the obstacle left the view or the path): the gap cue's own declared tolerance of missing frames (configs/obstacles/gap_cue.json max_gap_s 0.3 s). Version 4 used 0.5 s; scored, it held shifts into Straw Bale gates (19 of 120 checkpoint switches with more than 4 deg in their last 0.5 s). The longest gap between refreshing samples in the pillar-C approach of minus-fast6-vg-02 was 0.19 s
pilot_notes.commit_max_s: upper bound of one commitment: an obstacle first confirmed at about 6 m is passed within 1-2 s at 3-6 m/s; continued votes re-commit
pilot_notes.switch_votes: much stronger opposite evidence: this many CONSECUTIVE fresh opposite obstacle votes (confirmation needs 2 of 3), each of at least switch_min_deg
pilot_notes.switch_min_deg: half the shift clip, three times active_deg
pilot_notes.switch_window_s: enough time to complete the switch: a switch is allowed only this long after the commitment began, before the vehicle has responded to it; 0.3 s is the fast PD's declared response delay (brain-08: 0.55 s), the shorter and so more conservative bound. Later opposite confirmations are blocked (counted) until the commitment is released; after the release the side latch holds as after any confirmation
pilot_notes.terrain_yields: obstacle votes take priority over terrain votes (as version 2 declared): a terrain episode never latches out an obstacle confirmation on the other side. In minus-fast6-vg-02 version 2's side latch of a terrain episode blocked the pillar-C obstacle evidence for 0.6 s
pilot_notes.terrain_rising_only: with a vertical guard declared (configs/obstacles/vertical_guard.json), terrain votes count only while the guard's climb is for confirmed rising ground (its escalated stage); not while it arrests a descent or climbs gently for the floor below a sinking path. The terrain side steer was designed for the Pine Valley mound; in 6 of 8 Minus Two stack flights it fired in the garage, and in minus-fast6-vg-02 it steered 6 deg toward pillar C for 0.7 s. Without a vertical guard version 2's rule (any governor climb) is kept. In shadow the guard's shadow copy decides
pilot_notes.commit_occluded: false: an 'occluded' decision (the ring column itself near) does not START a commitment (it still refreshes and grows one). Its side is the nearest observed-free column, which flips between frames, and the near object may be the ring's own gate: at Straw Bale gates the inflatable arch's top crosses the band at the ring 1-1.5 s before the gate (+-12 deg flicker), and in store run 129 an occluded frame at the checkpoint before Minus Two pillar A committed version 4 to the pillar side. The pillar-C commitment started on one-sided 'gap' evidence. Version 4 behaved as true

runtime_notes.placement: camera: in the camera process after the checkpoint cue and looming; process: a separate depth process fed by a one-frame slot right after capture (resize, masks and depth run while the camera computes the cue; the decision waits for that frame's cue, which the camera copies into the slot). The depth process sets its own priority class to above normal like the camera process (spawned before the runner raises its class, it would otherwise inherit the runner's below normal under Anode), and the camera never waits for it: the camera's side of the slot takes its locks without blocking (a busy slot skips that frame or cue, counted) and signals with semaphores; the depth process writes its samples to its own shared array (read by the controller without blocking) and stops on its own event, so it takes no lock or event of the camera's. process was chosen by the G8 runtime bench (configs/obstacles/gap_bench_gates.json v1, sha256 db551b8813a3..., straw-brain08-06 30-90 s replayed with Liftoff idle, version 1 runtime: depth process at the bench parent's normal class, cue read from the camera's shared memory): camera failed (14.6 Hz < 15, gap age p95 173 ms > 150), process passed (17.9 Hz, loop p95 68.3 ms, gap age p95 113 ms, checkpoint-cue latency p95 +0.1 ms over the baseline, fp16 vs fp32 0.14% p95). The version 2 runtime is re-benched from a below-normal parent (docs/obstacle_gap_pilot.md)
runtime_notes.stride: 1: every camera frame; 2: every other frame

change: v5: a disclosed revision after version 4 was scored on the frozen gates configs/obstacles/gap_commit_gates.json version 2 (results docs/experiments/gap_commit_v4_results.json): pillar C passed (right confirmed 0.99 s before the impact and held, no shift toward the pillar), but S (Straw Bale switch quietness 101/120 against >= 95%) and A (store run 129: a pillar-side commitment, 147 right ticks against 33, 17 ticks aimed into the pillar) failed, and B failed for version 2 too (0.95 s against 1.0 s at the pilot level). Version 5 changes two values: commit_hold_s 0.5 -> 0.3 (the gap cue's max_gap_s) and commit_occluded false (pilot_notes). Chosen after reading the version 4 results and three development variants on the same data (occluded alone: S 113/120; the hold alone: S 105/120 and store run 129 still failing; both: S 115/120), so every gate data set is development data for version 5, not held-out. Version 4's change note: v4: version 3's rules with one correction, before any gate was scored: in version 3 only same-side votes and close samples without a vote refreshed the commitment, so sustained opposite votes weaker than the switch rule released it after commit_hold_s and, after the side latch, let the other side take over: a switch on weaker evidence, against the rule's intent (hold the side while the obstacle stays ahead; switch only on much stronger opposite evidence early enough). A unit test found it. Version 4 refreshes the hold on any obstacle vote or close sample. Parameters unchanged. Version 3's change note: v3 (round 4, pillar C of Minus Two): minus-fast6-vg-02 hit pillar C (the next ring lies 1.1 m beside its free, right edge) after (1) the terrain side steer, driven by the vertical guard's gentle floor climb after the hairpin, aimed 6 deg LEFT, toward the pillar, for 0.7 s; (2) version 2's side latch of that terrain episode blocked the gap cue's RIGHT obstacle evidence (first vote 1.05 s before the impact) for 0.6 s; (3) the right shift, confirmed 0.39 s before the impact, came too late. Version 3 adds commit (side commitment near an obstacle), terrain_yields and terrain_rising_only (pilot_notes). Every version 2 value and the runtime are unchanged; with the three switches off the gap aim is version 2's, bit for bit.
